source.title: When Bad Data Leads to Good Models
source.authors: Kenneth Li; Yida Chen; Fernanda Viégas; M. Wattenberg

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and measures feature-direction entanglement and toxicity separability, but it does not audit neuron poles, test explanations on held-out activations, score automated neuron explanations, or build attribution graphs from neurons.
record.gate_note: No result tests the stated neuron-pole job shares or the claim versions about neuron explanations. The paper's own feature-direction entanglement and toxicity-probe findings are adjacent to the claim's subject, so they are recorded under versions ["none"]. Background statements about neurons encoding multiple concepts cite other work and are not recorded as study results. Figure 3's numerical values are not given in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature-direction entanglement in a toy transformer and linear toxicity-probe accuracy in attention heads of Olmo-1B under varied pretraining data. It never audits neuron poles, scores neuron explanations, builds neuron attribution graphs, or revisits InceptionV1 neurons. Superposition appears only as background and motivation, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also report that toxic data yields less entangled toxicity representations and better probe accuracy. A 10% toxic-data share gave the best detoxification trade-off under ITI, prompting, SFT and DPO, and lower GCG attack success.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies pretraining data composition, feature-direction entanglement, and detoxification; it does not use a neuron-pole auditing or explanation-testing recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: In the toy experiment, feature entanglement changes with the underrepresented feature's data contribution. In Olmo-1B, the reported probe comparison is C4 only versus 25% 4chan; the paper also reports detoxification outcomes varying with toxic-data proportion, but those do not test the listed neuron-interpretability versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 4-layer toy transformer with a 4-dimensional residual stream, the underrepresented feature's entanglement drops as its training-data share rises. It approaches the other features' average entanglement of about 0.8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How often a feature appears in training data affects how entangled (superposed) its representation direction is.

fits_no_version.finding: In Olmo-1B, adding 25% 4chan data to pretraining raises mean toxicity-probe accuracy across attention heads (p = 0.0002) and gives a fatter right tail of high-accuracy heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Toxic pretraining data yields more linearly separable toxicity representations in attention heads.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: The toy experiment is very small (4-dimensional residual stream) and Figure 3's exact values are not stated in the text. The probe result reports a difference and confidence interval but not absolute mean accuracies. The experiments use Olmo-1B and do not assess neuron-pole explanations.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted because the paper's detoxification, generation-toxicity, capability, and jailbreak outcomes do not measure neuron jobs or explanation fidelity. The verbalization token counts are also not neuron-interpretability measures.

untested.parts: All of it. The data-composition effect on entanglement concerns directions, not neuron interpretability shares.

record.verdict_notes: This is an off-topic study on pretraining data composition and detoxification. Its superposition framing is background, citing Elhage et al. 2022, and it makes no neuron-level interpretability measurement.

versions.untested_parts: Shares across model families, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability shares across architectures, regularization, and tools.
Neuron-based attribution graphs and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict firing on new examples.
Automated neuron-explanation scores on new text.

rows.subject: Olmo-1B
rows.size_stated: 1B parameters; 24 layers, 16 attention heads per layer, hidden size 1024
rows.operation_detail: Trained linear classifiers on last-token attention-head activations to classify ToxiGen toxicity labels; compared validation accuracy distributions.
rows.measure: Mean validation accuracy of toxicity probes across attention heads and layers
rows.baseline: Olmo-1B trained on C4 only; absolute accuracy not stated
rows.value: The 25%-4chan model had higher average accuracy; difference 95% CI [0.67, 1.18]
rows.uncertainty: p = 0.0002; 95% confidence interval for the difference [0.67, 1.18]
rows.note: The paper reports a higher average probe accuracy and a fatter right tail for the toxic-data model. It does not report the absolute average accuracies in the text.
rows.check: This row compares probe accuracy on attention heads, not neuron interpretability, so no version applies. The 'observed' state refers only to the study's own hypothesis. The CI [0.67, 1.18] is presumably in percentage points; the unit is not stated.
